[Policy: Guide to Choosing Classes] [Section: Credit Requirements]

Exchange students are normally required to select classes totalling 60 Strathclyde credits per semester, which is equivalent to 30 ECTS credits.

[Policy: Guide to Choosing Classes] [Section: Class Levels]

Exchange students usually choose classes from levels one to three, which correspond to first to third year at Strathclyde. Level four classes are not normally available unless the student has significant prior knowledge, sufficient space is available in the class, and approval is granted by the host department.

[Policy: Guide to Choosing Classes] [Section: Flexibility and Changes]

Applicants are strongly advised to remain flexible with their class choices, as changes may be required after arrival at Strathclyde due to availability or academic considerations.

[Policy: Guide to Choosing Classes] [Section: Where to Find Class Lists]

Lists of classes available to exchange students are provided by individual departments and through the University module catalogue. Students should consult the official guide for the most up-to-date department-specific class lists and contact details.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Application Workflow Overview]

The exchange application follows a structured, step-by-step workflow. Applicants must complete each stage of the application in sequence, and progress to later stages is not possible until earlier sections have been completed. The workflow provides a clear overview of application status and progress.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Personal and Address Details]

As part of the exchange application, students are required to complete their personal information and permanent home address details. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that all information provided is accurate and up to date before proceeding to subsequent stages of the application.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Required Supporting Documents]

Applicants must upload a set of supporting documents as part of the exchange application. These typically include a current authenticated academic transcript, an English translation of the transcript where applicable, and a copy of the passport identification page. Documents must be provided in approved digital formats, such as PDF or Word.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Document Quality and Translation Requirements]

All supporting documents must meet quality and authenticity requirements. Academic transcripts must be official and authenticated. Where documents are not originally in English, a fully certified English translation is required. Translations must be professionally produced and verifiable, including confirmation of accuracy, translator identification, and contact details. Non-English documents submitted without an appropriate translation will be rejected.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Course and Class Selection]

Applicants are required to submit a provisional list of courses or classes as part of their exchange application. Course information must include unit codes, titles, and credit values. At Strathclyde, 20 Strathclyde credits are equivalent to 10 ECTS credits. Submitted course selections are reviewed by the Exchange Team and forwarded to the relevant academic department for approval.

[Policy: Exchange Application Process] [Section: Approval Outcomes and Next Steps]

Following submission, applications are reviewed by the Exchange Team and the relevant academic department. If all proposed courses are approved, applicants receive confirmation by email along with an official approval notice. If any courses are not approved, applicants are informed of the reason and invited to submit alternative course selections for further review.

[Policy: Academic Credit Guidance] [Section: Credit Load Per Semester]

Students are normally expected to take 60 Strathclyde credits (equivalent to 30 ECTS credits) per semester. Taking more than the recommended credit load is discouraged, as experience has shown that students who exceed this limit may struggle academically. Students who wish to discuss alternative arrangements or exceptional circumstances are advised to contact the Exchange Team at incoming.exchanges@strath.ac.uk.

[Policy: Student Visa Guidance] [Section: Visa Requirement Check]

Students planning to study in the UK for less than six months may not require a visa, depending on their nationality and circumstances. Students are advised to use the UK Government’s official ‘Check if I need a visa’ tool to confirm their individual visa requirements.

[Policy: Student Visa Guidance] [Section: Student Visa Overview]

Students planning to study at the University of Strathclyde for more than six months are normally required to hold a Student visa. The Student visa replaced the Tier 4 visa in October 2020 and applies to international students, including those from the EU, EEA, Switzerland, and other countries. Visa requirements vary, and students should consult official guidance for up-to-date information.
